gaps: K1: Uses relationship on the indexed expression (xs[i] reads/writes emit no Uses on xs)
K2: Calls relationship for constructor delegation (constructor(x) : super(x) / this(1) emit no Calls)
K3: Type reference for Foo::bar callable references (no reference to Foo emitted)
K4: Uses relationship for string-template identifiers ("hi $name" emits no Uses on name)
K5: typealias Fn = (Int) -> String emits no symbol
K6: object : Runnable2 { ... } emits no reference to the implemented type and misattributes inner methods to the enclosing class
K7: init { } / by lazy { } / field-initializer calls emit with source "Global" instead of the enclosing type (call exists, attribution wrong)
K8: import edges mislabeled: isImportDep flag not recognized by the tier classifier -> import_based never applied (reference_qualified instead); kotlin/scala confirmed finding from the java pass

K9: the generic-substitution mirror diverged from the judge on the NULLABLE spelling of a type variable: hasTypeVar split the signature on `,` and required the whole token to be one capital letter, so `(T?)` — how Kotlin writes every generic parameter — read as a CONCRETE type. The exact-signature test then failed AND the documented name-only fallback never fired, so an override whose DECLARING ancestor is a GRANDPARENT interface fell through to the first-supertype guess. Measured on exposed-core ColumnType.kt (`ColumnWithTransform : ColumnType`, `ColumnType : IColumnType`, `IColumnType.valueToDB sig=(T?)`): the analyzer published `ColumnType.valueToDB` at 0.5 — a type that declares no such member — where the truth says `IColumnType.valueToDB`. Four such rows, and they were the oracle-sharpness sweep's first HARD masks on a lane other than groovy (#949).
